column1: # Class relaxation rules for the shapes pipeline (see relaxation/RelaxationRules.kt and
# Format: class.name<TAB>level<TAB>reason (reason is required — say WHICH
# merge the rule unblocks; a rule is a conscious decision to hide something).
#   class-only                (analyzer) only the class matters; children
#                             concealed from the key, stay in scope
#                             on an SCC member it quotients the WHOLE SCC
#                             because an SCC is one strongly-connected object
#                             and member multiplicity is a children-list fact
#   conceal-field:<name>      (extraction) drop this named field of the class
#                             and all subclasses — the edge never enters the
#                             graph; the surgical choice for a lazy/cache
# The class column may instead be `regex:<pattern>` — a FULL-match regex
# against class names, consulted only when no exact rule matches; the first
# matching regex in file order wins, and a regex matching no class in the
# graph warns like an unknown exact class. Use a regex for namespace-wide
# policies over open-ended class sets (generated species/lambda classes),
# not to save typing on two or three stable names. conceal-field requires
# Rules on abstract classes cover the runtime _Decorated subclasses (exact
# class hierarchy from the dump). hprof-analyze applies field rules during
# extraction and class rules during analysis in the same JVM.

column3: With vs without an instantiated InternalHttpClient (cold-cache first resolutions vs warmed) splits per-module resolver chains; the merge is blocked only below this object (verified: run-jfr-38 retained set, SHP1 diffs terminate here)

Lazy field (Gradle ExternalResourceResolver.kt:290 create-on-first-use): set only where a real artifact download happened (cold-cache first resolutions), null elsewhere; its presence splits the UserResolverChain SCC. Field-level concealment drops exactly this edge — the AR objects leave the scope; everything else about MavenResolver stays exact. Verified: chain SCCs merge, 181 content groups unchanged (run-jfr-38)

description is UI text, not structure. The six alphabetically-first modules share their configuration description Strings with the IDEA tooling model (sync OOM'd mid-model-build), which cuts those Strings from their retained sets and splits their SCCs (String×5/6 missing). Concealing the field removes the split AND the uniform noise: every module's SCC loses the description edges identically. Verified: the six modules merge into their population groups (run-jfr-38)

Traced via a pair diff (run-jfr-38 debugUnitTestRuntimeClasspath :api:f0-api vs :api:f939-api, ndirect 2 vs 3): the single origin divergence was this object's writeIndex HashMap (155+ndirect same-shaped entries, mult 157 vs 158 on the projected table). Per the Gradle source it is a per-serialization-pass dedup index over ComponentSelectors ("should not be reused to serialize multiple graphs") — its fill level records HOW the serialization walk proceeded, not WHAT the configuration contains. Transient infrastructure: concealed from StreamingResolutionResultBuilder; the map, the readIndex list and the delegate stay in scope with exact counts.

Resolved dependency-closure contents (including cardinality) are intentionally excluded from configuration shape identity. artifactsById contains one ArtifactSet per visited graph node, so closure sizes split otherwise identical configuration SCCs (the 24-member lint-classpath SCC family: 102 -> 10 shapes; root shapes: 268 -> 81 on run-jfr-38). This is a targeted owner rule, unlike rejected Object[] set-children: resolution objects stay in scope with exact counts, but their contents no longer propagate into referrer keys.

DefaultConfiguration.currentResolveState is a second path from configuration SCCs to the resolved graph, resolved configuration and artifact-selection services; concealing DefaultVisitedArtifactResults alone leaves those closure differences in the key. Class-only conceals the cached result while preserving Optional empty/present state and all children/counts. With DefaultSelectedArtifactSet below: 1713 -> 1656 shapes, 81 -> 78 root shapes, no previous root shape splits (run-jfr-38).

ResolutionResultProviderBackedSelectedArtifactSet.delegate is the other resolved-content path: exactly isomorphic 46-member configuration SCCs still had different resolved graph results and empty vs five-entry resolved artifact lists. Class-only conceals selection contents while preserving delegate null/present and all children/counts; declared dependencies and registered collection actions still split. Verified with DefaultResolverResults: :classpath 5 -> 4, incomingCatalogForLibs0 2 -> 1, kotlinBuildToolsApiClasspath 3 -> 2 variants (run-jfr-38).

java.lang.invoke block, whole namespace: per-call-site JIT/lambda plumbing whose identity is generated-code position, not program data (5,943 rows / 112k objects on run-jfr-38 v9 across LambdaForm/Name/NamedFunction, BoundMethodHandle species, DirectMethodHandle variants, MethodType/MethodTypeForm, MemberName, Invokers, wrappers). A regex because the set is open-ended: species and $$Lambda capture classes are generated per dump. Handles and IR stay in scope with exact counts; the two set-children array rules below override this regex for their classes.
Same block: with Name leafed the IR arrays differ only by instruction count (782 rows on run-jfr-38 v9) - a code-size fact, not data.
Same block: handle tables differ only by slot counts once handles are leafed (21 rows on run-jfr-38 v9).

JFR block, whole namespace: the live recorder's per-event-type registry (EventType/PlatformEventType/EventControl/Control/settings/metadata, ~2,600 rows on run-jfr-38 v13) is recorder self-configuration - code, not data; the parsed recording the daemon retains (RecordedEvent 196,107 objects, RecordedStackTrace 976 rows / 6,399 objects, consumer parser machinery) is recording content, where per-event/per-trace identity is like splitting strings by characters. Exact-line equivalent measured 56,630 -> 49,025 shapes. Objects and bytes stay exact, so the retained recording still reads as a mass finding.
One entries-list per enum class, keyed by its constants (307 rows / 333 objects): class metadata like Class objects themselves; the enum constants keep their own rows.

Kotlin lazy cells: SynchronizedLazyImpl has lock=this, so every cell is a self-loop SCC keyed by initialization state - UNINITIALIZED_VALUE sentinel vs computed value, plus a per-call-site initializer $$Lambda nulled after init (123+31+8+2 rows / 244,616 objects across the four Lazy impls on run-jfr-38 v11). Lazy-init presence is not structure; values stay in scope with exact counts.

Guava cache block: a cache is transient infrastructure and its per-instance identity is fill state, not structure. Covers the wrappers (LocalManualCache/LocalLoadingCache: segment tables/queues initialize lazily on writes - 12 singleton SCC shapes vs one 38,994-instance shape inside resolver chains on run-jfr-38), the guts (LocalCache+Segment per-cache SCCs keyed by contents, 28 rows / 234,198 objects on v12), and entries/value references (StrongEntry 37 rows / 171,453 objects, StrongValueReference 85 rows / 226,121 objects, weak/soft variants whose entry back-references form SCCs). Cached objects stay in scope and keep their counts. The AccessQueue set-children rule below overrides this regex to normalize flattened LRU ring sizes.

Guava LRU ring, flattened at extraction to its member set: the member count is the segment fill level (66 ring SCC rows / 11,254 objects on run-jfr-38 v12), a children-list fact once members are uniform leaves via the cache regex rule (exact rules win over regexes).

Kotlin renderer config in both embedded compiler copies: an options object plus ~50 vetoable property delegates form one SCC per renderer, keyed by option values (30 rows / 1,618 objects on run-jfr-38 v11). Tooling configuration, not heap data.

Compiled regex block, whole namespace: a Pattern object graph is a compiled automaton - code position, not program data (1,398 rows / 18,182 objects on run-jfr-38 v10; node next-chains make every program suffix its own shape). A regex because automaton node classes are many. The Pattern$Node[] set-children rule below overrides for branch tables; pattern strings and nodes stay in scope.
Compiled regex block: branch tables differ only by alternative counts once nodes are leafed (87 rows on run-jfr-38 v10).

Per-type registry block: reflection member descriptors - Method 142 rows / 13,092 objects, Constructor 102 rows / 37,613 objects on run-jfr-38 v16, split by generic-signature repositories and annotation blobs. Same category as Groovy's CachedMethod: a Method object describes code.
Per-type registry block: generated/method-handle accessors paired with the descriptors above (18-row Field accessor SCC family and friends on run-jfr-38 v16).
Per-type registry block: generic-signature repositories/factories behind Method/Constructor (24+16-row SCC families on run-jfr-38 v16).
Per-type registry block: Introspector bean-info cache - GenericBeanInfo 106 rows, MethodDescriptor[] 104 rows plus descriptor tails on run-jfr-38 v16; one descriptor tree per introspected class.
Per-type registry block: parsed .kotlin_metadata ProtoBuf messages (ProtoBuf$Class 127 rows, ProtoBuf$TypeTable 86 rows plus message tails on run-jfr-38 v16) - class metadata, not program data.
Per-type registry block: JPMS module descriptors/references, one per module (106 rows / 118 objects on run-jfr-38 v16).
Per-type registry block: kotlin compiler phase configuration objects, one per lowering phase (85 rows / 85 objects on run-jfr-38 v16).

Per-type registry block: Gradle serialization/configuration-cache plumbing - one Binding/TypeInfo/codec object per serializable type, plus encoder stream state and WriteIdentities dedup indexes (802 rows / 1,685 objects on run-jfr-38 v15; Binding alone 165 rows / 398 objects). Same category as the traced DeduplicatingComponentSelectorSerializer rule: how the serializer is wired records code structure, not what the build model contains. Serialized model objects live outside this namespace and keep their rows.

Per-type registry block: Groovy reflection cache - one CachedClass (plus $1..$n lazy holders, ClassInfo, stdclasses variants) per described class (228 rows / 10,001 objects on run-jfr-38 v15, mostly as 53+27+15-row SCC families). Mirror of the CachedMethod decision.
Per-type registry block: java serialization descriptors, one per serializable class incl. $ClassDataSlot arrays (99 rows / 278 objects on run-jfr-38 v15, largest family a 58-row SCC).
Per-type registry block: JAXB runtime reflection model - ClassBeanInfoImpl/LeafBeanInfoImpl/StructureLoader/XsiTypeLoader per bean class (~170 rows on run-jfr-38 v15 as 49/27-row SCC families).
Per-type registry block: kotlin/intellij PSI stub element types, one object per AST node type incl. per-type $$Lambda factories (110 rows on run-jfr-38 v15).

Groovy metaclass reflection cache: entries key per-class method lists (FastArray/CachedMethod trees), so each entry is its own shape (558 rows / 8,806 objects on run-jfr-38 v9 after chain normalization). The index mirrors loaded code, not program data; method objects stay in scope.
Same cache: per-method records with lazily-initialized parameter/class caches whose presence is warmup state (367 rows on run-jfr-38 v9); splits FastArrays and MetaBeanProperties per method.
Same cache: method-list holder (275 rows on run-jfr-38 v9); with CachedMethod leafed it differs only by its backing Object[] length.

Completes the IdeDependenciesCoreDirect/CoreRef decision below: the 31 surviving IdeDependencyCoreImpl shapes (2,587,120 objects on run-jfr-38 v17) are the alphabet over which every transitive-dependency list splits - 6,484 ArrayList/Object[] rows within three steps above this class are distinct multisets of those 31 symbols. Per-node identity of a dependency-graph mirror node is closure composition, which this policy already excludes; objects keep exact counts, lists collapse to per-length rows.

IDE-side mirror of the resolved-closure exclusion (DefaultVisitedArtifactResults rule): the dependency ITEMS collapse to 31 IdeDependencyCoreImpl shapes over 2.59M objects, so the 2,329 rows of this holder differ only in the per-module closure MULTISET (which of the 31, how many: list totals 188-242), and that single distinction fans out through artifacts/variants/models into ~12.7k rows (run-jfr-38 v8). Dependency composition is deliberately excluded from model identity; the lists and items stay in scope with exact counts.

Second path to the same closure data: CoreRef wraps a CoreDirect plus its own dependency list (1,116 distinct Direct + 912 distinct ArrayList children across 2,025 rows on run-jfr-38 v8); concealing Direct alone leaves the Ref split in referrer keys. Same policy, same accounting: contents stay in scope with exact counts.

Groovy parser ATN/DFA cache internals: a prediction context is a per-parse-position stack whose parent chain makes every suffix its own shape (2,002 rows over 10,879 objects with only 3 origin signatures on run-jfr-38), and no chain can merge while its tail differs. class-only makes contexts leaves so DFAState/ATNConfig referrers merge; contexts stay in scope with exact counts.

Same cache, merged-stack variant: parents is a PredictionContext[] of per-suffix members, so with SingletonPredictionContext leafed the remaining splits still propagate through nested ArrayPredictionContext parents (1,776 rows / 2,818 objects on run-jfr-38). class-only completes the chain cut; the parents arrays and their contexts stay in scope.

A configuration's strong core (the DefaultLegacyConfiguration+String+DefaultDomainObjectSet+ElementShadow SCC) carries exactly 7 identical members per direct project dependency (416+7*ndirect members, established by per-instance heap inspection in the root-cause analysis), so modules split purely by HOW MANY identical shadow members they have — a children-list fact: ndirect remains visible in the key through the distinct DefaultDependencySet/DefaultPublishArtifactSet members. set-children quotients the SCC (identical members dedupe) and normalizes child multiplicities; distinct declared dependency/artifact-set members still split, while resolved closure contents are excluded by the targeted rule above. Verified: 50/50 population merges preserved, implementation-family roles 12 -> 3 (run-jfr-38).

column3: Resolved dependency-graph mirror (MavenDependencyDescriptor, ModuleComponentIdentifier, configuration/variant metadata): per-module identity is closure composition over coordinates, the same registry policy as the Ide* model mirror. 451+48 rows / 2,267,134 objects on run-jfr-38, all hanging as exact-split satellites of the 138M-object provider SCC fringe.

Dependency-resolution machinery and result model (ivyservice state, resolution results, configuration internals): a per-build registry keyed by module coordinates; row-per-resolved-node is the composition split already excluded by policy. 505 rows / 3,615,570 objects on run-jfr-38. Exact rules above (DefaultLegacyConfiguration set-children etc.) still win over this regex.
Attribute schema and ImmutableAttributes interning registry: per-attribute-set identity is a dictionary over attribute names, not object structure. 203 rows / 480,763 objects on run-jfr-38.

Provider/Property cells (ValueState, DefaultMapProperty, FixedValueProvider): lazy-initialization state machines, the same policy as kotlin Lazy cells; 7 sibling DefaultMapProperty SCCs plus the giant ValueState component key on init-state otherwise. 249 rows / 8,984,490 objects on run-jfr-38; counts stay exact per class.
ProtocolToModelAdapter dynamic-proxy view graph: per-view identity mirrors whatever model it wraps (code, not data). 167 rows / 918,661 objects on run-jfr-38.

Virtual file-system snapshot trees (DirectorySnapshot, ChildMap variants): per-directory subtree identity splits the VFS mirror like a string split by characters; class rows keep exact node counts for VFS-bloat questions. 889 rows / 797,163 objects on run-jfr-38 (ChildMap$Entry 266, MediumChildMap 156, DirectorySnapshot 155).
FilteringClassLoader spec tries and classloader scaffolding: package-name tries are configuration, not heap structure. 148 rows / 1,650 objects on run-jfr-38.
AGP DSL/model/options trees: plugin configuration registry, per-option identity is composition. 1,022 rows / 579,267 objects on run-jfr-38, largest single family of the giant-SCC fringe.
Completes the Ide* model-mirror policy (IdeDependencyCoreImpl exact rules above still win): remaining per-node rows of the Android IDE sync model. 162 rows / 3,168,513 objects on run-jfr-38.
Kotlin Gradle plugin model/config trees (targets, source sets, tooling model): same plugin-registry category as AGP. 418 rows / 344,014 objects on run-jfr-38.

HTTP connection-pool internals: 83 pooled connections each carry an identical writer/buffer/parser trio, so the repetition count IS the finding and survives as exact class counts (DefaultHttpRequestWriter x83). 355 rows / 5,616 objects on run-jfr-38.
Gson TypeAdapter wiring: per-type codec graph is code, not data, same category as the serialization codecs above. 145 rows / 69,249 objects on run-jfr-38.

IntelliJ external-system sync model (ArtifactDependencyNode, ReferenceNode): a third dependency-graph mirror alongside the Ide* and gradle component models, same registry policy. 54+ alphabet rows touching 334 bottom-block collection rows on run-jfr-38.
JPMS ModuleDescriptor/Exports/Requires value objects: module metadata is code description, complements the jdk.internal.module rule above. 61+ rows touching 317 collection rows on run-jfr-38.
Gradle service registry and its ClassInspector reflection cache: per-service wiring is DI code, not data. 62 ClassDetails rows touching 194 collection rows on run-jfr-38.
DefaultModuleRegistry module/classpath catalog: a registry of gradle distribution jars. 58 DefaultModule rows touching 174 collection rows on run-jfr-38.

Groovy MOP metadata (MetaBeanProperty, MetaClassImpl and friends): per-property reflection descriptors, same category as org.codehaus.groovy.reflection; narrow Meta.* prefix deliberately spares Closure/GString user values. 9 rows touching 355 collection rows on run-jfr-38.
CodeSource/ProtectionDomain/certificate chains attached to every loaded class: classloading security metadata, not heap structure. 4 CodeSource rows touch 103 collection rows on run-jfr-38.
java.lang.Package and VersionInfo: per-package metadata of loaded code. 7 rows touching 102 collection rows on run-jfr-38.
Configuration-cache implementation state (ClassLoaderScopeSpec and serializer scaffolding): cache machinery, same category as the serialize codecs. 22 rows on run-jfr-38.

Persistent-cache in-memory machinery (BTreePersistentIndexedCache IndexEntry alphabet): per-entry file offsets split 264 collection rows above them on run-jfr-38; cache index identity is infrastructure.
Anonymous action wrapper: one wrapper per listener call site, identity mirrors the wrapped action (code). 75 rows / 237,338 objects on run-jfr-38 bottom block.
